title: What stays when six positive tokens leave five?
description: Five positive tokens sit on a tray, but six must be taken away. An extra zero pair is put out so six positive tokens can be lifted off, and one negative token stays. Keeko thinks putting out a zero pair changes the value.
teaching_notes: One idea: when the tray has too few tokens to take away, put out a zero pair, which does not change the value, and then take away. Watch for students who think the zero pair changes the value of the set.

source: Example: Let us subtract (+5) - (+6). Put down 5 positives. But there are not enough tokens to take out 6 positives! Put out an extra zero pair (a positive and a negative), which does not change the value of the set of tokens.
video_script.why: The child subtracts a larger number of positive tokens from a smaller one by putting out a zero pair first.
video_script.substitution: Put out as many zero pairs as are needed, lift off the tokens being subtracted, and read the answer from the tokens that stay.
video_script.anchor: a tray of five positive tokens
video_script.wrong_answer: putting out a zero pair changes the value
video_script.wrong_move: thinks that adding a zero pair to the tray changes the value of the set of tokens
video_script.payoff_line: Positive five take away positive six leaves negative one.
maths_rules: (+5) is 5 positive tokens; 6 positive tokens must be taken out, but only 5 are there
1 positive and 1 negative token make a zero pair: (+1) + (−1) = 0, so the value stays 5
with 1 zero pair the tray holds 6 positive and 1 negative token; take out 6 positive tokens
video_script.design: One idea: put out a zero pair so enough tokens are on the tray, then take away. Positive tokens are green and negative tokens are red as in the book. Keeko's doubt is that the zero pair changes the value.
